newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: Turkmens to export 40 bln cubic metres gas in '97.
newsitem.headline: Turkmens to export 40 bln cubic metres gas in '97.

text.p: Turkmenistan will nearly double natural gas exports to 40 billion cubic metres in 1997, up from 24 billion cubic metres in 1996, Turkmen President Saparmurat Niyazov said on state television on Wednesday.

"In 1997, in agreement with (Russia's) Gazprom, 20 billion cubic metres of natural gas will be exported to Europe," Niyazov said, adding: "A further 20 billion cubic metres of Turkmen gas will be received by our traditional clients, Ukraine and the Transcaucasus (republics)."

In November, the head of Russia's RAO Gazprom GAZP.RTS 0#GAZP.RUO, Rem Vyakhirev, said the desert nation would be able to export natural gas through its pipeline network to Europe but gave no details on volumes.
Exports of gas to western Europe are crucial for Turkmenistan's hard-hit economy,
Turkmenistan's gas, once exported to western Europe and its main export revenue earner, has been locked in Russian pipelines and diverted to other impoverished former Soviet republics who cannot pay.

The former Soviet republic, estimated to have one of the largest reserves of natural gas in the world, saw gas production in 1995 sink to 35.6 billion cubic metres from 63.5 billion cubic metres in 1993.
